about: Battery swapping and safety standards and the swap networks being built in India, with their status.

rows.name: IS 17896 Part 1: battery swap systems, general and guidance
rows.scope: Swapping of EV batteries with the powertrain off, up to 1,000 V AC and 1,500 V DC; based on IEC TS 62840-1

rows.name: IS 17896 Part 2: safety requirements
rows.scope: Safety of battery swap systems; based on IEC 62840-2
rows.status: Listed in Part 1 (status not stated there)

rows.name: IS 17896 Part 3: central management system for interoperable packs
rows.scope: How swap stations and interoperable packs are managed centrally

rows.name: IS 17896 Part 4: light electric vehicle battery swap
rows.scope: Pack dimensions, connectors and communication for two- and three-wheelers

rows.name: IS 17896 Part 5: heavy electric vehicle battery swap
rows.scope: Battery swapping for buses and trucks

rows.name: AIS-038 Rev 2: traction battery safety
rows.scope: Battery safety for electric buses and trucks; cells need valid IS 16893 test reports

rows.name: CATL standard swappable packs (#20, #25, #26 for cars, 75# for heavy trucks)
rows.scope: CATL says its standard packs fit about 85% of China's A-segment models; truck swaps take about 5 minutes vs about 25 at a charger

rows.name: EIM and HPCL swap-and-charge hubs for heavy trucks
rows.scope: Hubs on the Mumbai–Pune, Delhi–Jaipur and Chennai–Bangalore corridors over 18–24 months

rows.name: Blue Energy Motors and HPCL heavy e-truck swap station, Bhiwandi
rows.scope: On the Mumbai–Pune electric freight corridor; a swap takes under five minutes
